user.title: Quatt Heat Pump Configuration
user.description: Configure your Quatt heat pump data range and sensor entities.

data.temp_entities: Outside temperature sensor(s) — the first available one is used

gas.title: Gas Analysis (Optional)
gas.description: Configure gas consumption analysis to compare with heat pump performance. Use the period BEFORE your heat pump was installed.

options.title: Additional Options
options.description: Configure sensors and heating curve. The solar panel sensor can be any sensor that reports current power in Watts (W) — e.g. SolarEdge, Enphase, Huawei, SMA, or a template sensor. Leave empty if you have no solar panels.

data.indoor_temp_entity: Indoor temperature sensor (°C, for solar gain calibration)
data.sound_level_enabled: Enable soundslider control (limits the power through the soundslider of your Quatt)
data.sound_level_max_day: Soundslider: highest setting during the day
data.sound_night_start_hour: Soundslider: night starts at (hour, 0–23, e.g. 23) — same as the night times in the Quatt app
data.sound_night_end_hour: Soundslider: night ends at (hour, 0–23, e.g. 7) — same as the night times in the Quatt app
data.supply_temp_entity: Supply temperature sensor (°C) — reference for the advice

data_description.flow_entity: To convert power into supply temperature.
data_description.return_temp_entity: The advice starts from the return: supply = return + power / (1.16 × flow).
data_description.weather_entity: Outdoor temperature for the coming hours, for the look-ahead and the price shift.
data_description.indoor_temp_entity: For the room correction and the learning house model. Preferably a sensor in the living room.
data_description.sound_level_enabled: Controls the day and night setting of the soundslider in your Quatt.
data_description.sound_level_source: Start with Outdoor temperature + room. Choose Outdoor temperature if the room temperature or setpoint is not measured reliably. House model + room is for measuring whether the learning model steers better; it does not suit underfloor heating with a boiler that assists. The Steering effect card shows what works best for your house after a few weeks per setting.
data_description.sound_level_max_day: During the day the control never goes above this level, nor above your own level in the Quatt app. building87 is the quietest, normal the most powerful.
data_description.sound_level_max_night: At night the control never goes above this level, nor above your own level in the Quatt app. building87 is the quietest, normal the most powerful.
data_description.sound_night_start_hour: Local time, 0–23. Keep equal to the night times in the Quatt app: otherwise the integration controls the day setting while the Quatt is already on its night setting, or the other way round.
data_description.sound_night_end_hour: Local time, 0–23. Keep equal to the night times in the Quatt app.
data_description.supply_temp_entity: To compare the advice with, and to see whether the supply reaches the max supply temperature.

error.invalid_date_range: End date must be after start date
error.gas_entity_required: Gas entity is required when gas analysis is enabled

init.title: Update configuration
init.description: Grouped by topic. Collapsed sections are off or rarely needed. The heat demand to OpenQuatt (for Power House) is set up in OpenQuatt (the source helper), not here.

huis.name: House and comfort
huis.description: What the advice aims for, and what is set in your Quatt.

data.cic_rated_power: Rated power at −10 °C in your Quatt (W)

data_description.room_setpoint_fallback: Only used when the thermostat provides no setpoint (no OpenTherm link, or the source is briefly gone). When it does provide one, the thermostat wins.
data_description.comfort_floor_temp: Lowest acceptable indoor temperature. Reference for the safe coast time and stored heat, not the target temperature.
data_description.cic_zero_power_temp: CiC only, optional. Cannot be read: ask your installer or Quatt support. Empty = the advice shows only the recommended value.
data_description.cic_rated_power: CiC only, optional. As your installer set it. Empty = unknown.

max_aanvoertemperatuur.name: Max supply temperature
max_aanvoertemperatuur.description: Writes the advice plus the margin as maximum supply temperature to the controller at every interval: the CiC, or OpenQuatt outside Power House. Do not use with OpenQuatt in Power House: there this setting is a safety limiter; use the heat demand to OpenQuatt instead. On a CiC: use this or the soundslider control, not both at once.

data_description.ch_max_water_enabled: Writes the maximum supply temperature to your Quatt. Off = the integration writes nothing.
data_description.ch_max_water_source: Start with Outdoor temperature + room. Choose Outdoor temperature if the room temperature or setpoint is not measured reliably. House model + room is for measuring whether the learning model steers better; it does not suit underfloor heating with a boiler that assists. The Steering effect card shows what works best for your house after a few weeks per setting.
data_description.ch_max_water_margin: The heat pump already throttles before the maximum supply temperature. Without a margin it delivers too little and the room cannot catch up. Default 2 °C.
data_description.ch_max_water_entity: The entity for the maximum supply temperature. Empty = automatic: the CiC, or OpenQuatt when it runs the outdoor units.
data_description.ch_max_water_hysteresis: Only write when the new value differs this much from the last one. Keeps the setting from changing at every small fluctuation.
data_description.ch_max_water_interval: How often the maximum supply temperature is updated.

soundslider.name: Soundslider control (CiC only)
soundslider.description: Limits the power through the sound level of your Quatt, day and night, until the supply matches the advice. CiC only. Use this or the max supply temperature, not both at once. Your own setting returns when you turn this off; a setting you change in the Quatt app while this is on is set back within ten minutes.

data_description.sound_level_enabled: Controls the day and night setting of the soundslider in your Quatt.
data_description.sound_level_source: Start with Outdoor temperature + room. Choose Outdoor temperature if the room temperature or setpoint is not measured reliably. House model + room is for measuring whether the learning model steers better; it does not suit underfloor heating with a boiler that assists. The Steering effect card shows what works best for your house after a few weeks per setting.
data_description.sound_level_max_day: During the day the control never goes above this level, nor above your own level in the Quatt app. building87 is the quietest, normal the most powerful.
data_description.sound_level_max_night: At night the control never goes above this level, nor above your own level in the Quatt app. building87 is the quietest, normal the most powerful.
data_description.sound_night_start_hour: Local time, 0–23. Keep equal to the night times in the Quatt app: otherwise the integration controls the day setting while the Quatt is already on its night setting, or the other way round.
data_description.sound_night_end_hour: Local time, 0–23. Keep equal to the night times in the Quatt app.

prijsverschuiving.name: Price shift (shadow measurement)
prijsverschuiving.description: Calculates what shifting the heat demand to cheaper hours would have saved. Controls nothing.

data_description.price_shift_mode: Off, fixed (normal and off-peak) or dynamic. Off = no sensor.
data_description.price_entity: Dynamic tariff only: a sensor with today's and tomorrow's hourly prices as an attribute.
data_description.price_dal_weekend: Saturday and Sunday count entirely as off-peak.

analyse.name: Analysis
analyse.description: Which period of your heating history is analysed, and what is left out.

data_description.quatt_start_date: The heating history is analysed from this date: heat loss, heating curve and knee point.
data_description.performance_baseline_date: Did you change something in the control? Then the efficiency measure freezes its norm on everything before it and tests the days after against it. Empty = the last 30 heating days.
data_description.quatt_cloud_enabled: Off = local only (recorder and own storage). The built-up history stays; only new hourly detail stops. Mainly useful with a second local source such as OpenQuatt.
data_description.eos_throttle_entity: Optional. An entity indicating that an external controller is capping the heat pump, for example tariff control. Those periods are left out of the COP and heat-loss analysis. Empty = off.

metingen.name: Measurements
metingen.description: Which sensors the integration uses. Leave empty = automatic: whatever provides a value now, from Quatt or OpenQuatt. Only fill in when auto-detection picks the wrong one.

data.pv_power_entity: Sun sensor: PV power (W or kW)

data_description.temp_entities: One or more sensors; the first one with a value is used.
data_description.power_entity: The delivered heat. Basis of the heat loss and the COP.
data_description.power_input_entity: For the COP and the electricity use in the steering effect.
data_description.flow_entity: To convert power into supply temperature.
data_description.supply_temp_entity: To compare the advice with, and to see whether the supply reaches the max supply temperature.
data_description.return_temp_entity: The advice starts from the return: supply = return + power / (1.16 × flow).
data_description.boiler_heat_entity: To see when the boiler helps out.
data_description.indoor_temp_entity: For the room correction and the learning house model. Preferably a sensor in the living room.
data_description.room_setpoint_entity: The target the advice aims for.
data_description.control_setpoint_entity: The supply temperature the thermostat asks for over OpenTherm.
data_description.cop_entity: If your installation provides a COP itself.
data_description.compressor_entity: Compressor starts are counted from this.
data_description.compressor_2_entity: Duo only; leave empty on a Solo.
data_description.weather_entity: Outdoor temperature for the coming hours, for the look-ahead and the price shift.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Optional. Measures the sun locally. The orientation of panels and windows is learned, not asked.

error.price_entity_required: A dynamic tariff needs a price sensor with hourly prices as attributes

run_analysis.name: Run Warmteanalyse
run_analysis.description: Runs the full analysis pipeline: fetches data, calculates heating curves, COP, and heat loss.

update_dashboard.name: Restore dashboard
update_dashboard.description: Overwrites the Quatt Warmteanalyse dashboard with the version shipped by the integration. Any changes you made to that dashboard are lost. If you deleted the dashboard, this creates it again.

dashboard_update_available.title: New version of the Quatt Warmteanalyse dashboard

init.title: Dashboard update available
init.description:
This update ships an improved dashboard, but yours differs from the version the integration last wrote — so it was left untouched.

Choose what should happen. Either way this notice will not come back for this version.

menu_options.update: Take the new dashboard (my own changes to it are lost)
menu_options.keep: Keep my dashboard and stop asking

dashboard_create_failed.title: Quatt Warmteanalyse dashboard could not be created
dashboard_create_failed.description:
The integration could not create its dashboard automatically on this version of Home Assistant.

Create it yourself: go to **Settings → Dashboards → Add dashboard**, choose **New dashboard from scratch**, and set the URL to `{url_path}` (the title is up to you). Leave it empty. On the next restart, or when you reload the integration, it fills the dashboard and keeps it up to date from then on.

supply_sensor_offset.title: Supply temperature sensor is off
supply_sensor_offset.description:
The supply temperature ({supply_entity}) reads {offset} K compared with the water outlet of the heat pump ({reference_entity}), measured over {hours} hours of steady heating. Between those two points the water temperature hardly changes, so the sensor is off. The supply advice and the error sensors appear shifted by the same amount.

Using OpenQuatt? Run the water sensor calibration and check **Water Supply Temperature Calibration Status**. Without OpenQuatt, check how the supply sensor is mounted.

This notice disappears on its own once the difference drops below {clear} K.

options.stooklijn: Outdoor temperature — uses only the outdoor temperature, along your house's heat-loss line; does not know whether the room is warm enough (was Heating curve)
options.mpc: Outdoor temperature + room — the same line, higher when the room is below the setpoint and lower when above; the starting point (was MPC)
options.1r1c: House model + room — the learning house model (heat loss, current sun, constant heat gain) with the same room correction; steers like Outdoor temperature + room while the model is still learning (was House model (1R1C))
